rationale: Registered Parkinson ginger programs use powder tablets or two extract strengths and give no posted dyskinesia result. An inventor patent reports less abnormal involuntary movement with dried-rhizome extract in levodopa-treated mice, and the isolated zingerone observations gave no observed suppression. The animal preparation, disclosed methods and opposite results across compounds leave ground ginger and clinical dyskinesia unresolved.

Controlled processed-ginger trials in other populations generally favor constipation scores or frequency. Parkinson mixed formulas give mixed results, and the inventor patent reports fecal-water changes with isolated shogaol in mice. The Parkinson ginger trial registers GIDS-PD but has no posted item outcomes. The minimal lean against worsening relies on processed preparations and other populations.

A randomized craniotomy study's supplement gives inconclusive patient anxiety VAS comparisons for ginger extract. Root powder results in healthy adults are inconclusive and the SSRI adjunct abstract conflicts with itself about direction. The Parkinson extract trial has no posted item results. Rat extract studies offer indirect behavior data. Grated ginger and clinical Parkinson anxiety remain unresolved.

Mean fatigue rose 3.7 points in 14 Parkinson study completers after three months of brewed green tea. The same-cohort thesis provides no paired scores or exact p value. This uncontrolled comparison supports a minimal worsening lean. A postoperative randomized trial favored less fatigue. A fermented-tea crossover in healthy adults reports a smaller fatigue rise without a clear individual subscale estimate.
